message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| **1978** | *Halloween* (John Carpenter) | The original slasher that set the template for the genre. |
| **1980** | *The Shining* (Stanley Kubrick) | A psychological horror masterpiece based on Stephen King’s novel. |
| **1984** | *A Nightmare on Elm Street* (Wes Craven) | Introduces Freddy Krueger and the terrifying concept of dreams as a battlefield. |
| **1991** | *The Silence of the Lambs* (Jonathan Demme) | A tense thriller with iconic performances by Anthony Hopkins and Jodie Foster. |
| **1999** | *The Blair Witch Project* (Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Pioneered the found‑footage style and created a new wave of horror. |
| **2002** | *28 Days Later* (Danny Boyle) | A fast‑moving, post‑apocalyptic horror that revitalized the zombie sub‑genre. |
| **2004** | *Saw* (James Wan & Leigh Whannell) | A gritty, puzzle‑based horror that spawned a long‑running franchise. |
| **2007** | *Paranormal Activity* (Oren Peli) | Low‑budget found‑footage film that became a massive hit. |
| **2010** | *The Conjuring* (James Wan) | A chilling, well‑crafted supernatural horror that launched a franchise. |
| **2012** | *The Cabin in the Woods* (Dennis Dugan & Joss Whedon) | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and scary. |
| **2014** | *It Follows* (David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept with a unique visual style. |
| **2015** | *The Witch* (Robert Eggers) | A slow‑burning, atmospheric horror set in 1630s New England. |
| **2017** | *Get Out* (Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine scares. |
| **2018** | *Hereditary* (Ari Aster) | A deeply unsettling psychological horror that’s both beautiful and brutal. |
| **2019** | *Midsommar* (Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that turns the genre on its head with vivid, unsettling imagery. |
| **2020** | *The Invisible Man* (Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling of the classic tale with strong feminist undertones. |
| **2021** | *A Quiet Place Part II* (John Krasinski) | A tense, sound‑driven horror that builds on the original’s premise. |
| **2022** | *The Black Phone* (Scott Derrickson) | A supernatural thriller that blends creepy atmosphere with a compelling story. |
| **2023** | *M3GAN* (David Freyer) | A horror‑comedy about a lifelike doll that goes rogue. |
| **2024** | *The Last Voyage of the Demeter* (David Bruckner) | A fresh take on the Dracula mythos with a focus on claustrophobic dread. |

Feel free to pick a few from different eras or sub‑genres to keep your horror marathon varied and exciting!
